description: The Decree of Canopus was issued in 238 BC during the reign of Ptolemy III Euergetes and Queen Berenice II. Promulgated by a council of Egyptian priests, the decree honored the royal family, established new religious observances, and attempted to reform the Egyptian calendar by adding an extra day every four years—an early form of a leap-year system. Written in hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Greek, it also illustrates how the Ptolemaic monarchy blended Greek royal authority with traditional Egyptian religious institutions to strengthen its legitimacy.
